title: Receipt & Acknowledgement
text:
Receipt & Acknowledgement
Of our office Employee Manual
This Employee Manual is an important document intended to help you
become acquainted with our office. This Manual will serve as a guide; it is
not the final word in all cases. Individual circumstances may call for
individual attention.
Because the general business atmosphere of our office and economic
conditions are always changing, the contents of this Manual may be changed
at any time at the discretion of our office. No changes in any benefit, policy
or rule will be made without due consideration of the mutual advantages,
disadvantages, benefits and responsibilities such changes will have on you as
an employee and on our office.
Please read the following statements and sign below to indicate your receipt
and acknowledgement of Smile Studio Dentistry Employee Manual.
U I have received and read a copy of Smile Studio Dentistry Employee
Manual. I understand that the policies, rules and benefits described in it are
subject to change at the sole discretion of our office at any time.
U I further understand that my employment is terminable at will, either by
myself or our office, regardless of the length of my employment or the
granting of benefits of any kind, including but not limited to profit sharing
benefits which provide for vesting based upon length of employment.
U I understand that no contract of employment other than 'at will" has
been expressed or implied, and that no circumstances arising out of my
employment will alter my 'at will" employment relationship unless
expressed in writing, with the understanding specifically set forth and signed
by myself and Smile Studio Dentistry.
U I am aware that during the course of my employment confidential
information will be made available to me, i.e., customer lists, pricing
policies and other related information. I understand that this information is
critical to the success of Smile Studio Dentistry and must not be
disseminated or used outside of our office's premises. In the event of
termination of employment, whether voluntary or involuntary, I hereby
agree not to utilize or exploit this information with any other individual or
company.

title: We're very happy to welcome you to our office. Thank you for joining us!
text:
We're very happy to welcome you to our office. Thank you for joining us!
We want you to feel that your association with Smile Studio Dentistry will
be a mutually beneficial and pleasant one.
You have joined an organization that has established an outstanding
reputation for quality dentistry. Credit for this goes to every one of our
employees. We hope you, too, will find satisfaction and take pride in your
work here.
This Manual provides answers to most of the questions you may have about
Smile Studio Dentistry benefit programs, as well as the company policies
and procedures we abide by, our responsibilities to you and your
responsibilities to. If anything is unclear, please discuss the matter with your
manager. You are responsible for reading and understanding this Employee
Manual, and your performance evaluations will reflect your adherence to our
policies. In addition to clarifying responsibilities, we hope this Employee
Manual also gives you an indication of my interest in the welfare of all that
work here.
From time to time, the information included in our Employee Manual may
change. Every effort will be made to keep you informed through suitable
lines of communication, including postings on the bulletin board and/or
meetings.
Compensation and personal satisfaction gained from doing a job well are
only some of the reasons most people work. Most likely, many other factors
count among your reasons for working, pleasant relationships and working
conditions, career development and promotion opportunities, and health
benefits are just a few. Our office is committed to doing its part to assure
you of a satisfying work experience.
I extend to you my personal best wishes for your success and happiness at
our office.
Sincerely,
Dr. Raul C Gonzalez, D.M.D

title: As a member of our offices team, you will be expected to contribute your
text:
As a member of our offices team, you will be expected to contribute your
talents and energies to improve the environment and quality of the company,
as well as the company services. In return, you will be given opportunities to
grow and advance in your career
1. To provide our customers with the best quality with the best service.
2. To provide you with wages and benefits comparable to others doing
similar work within the industry in this region.
At our office, we always put safety first. We believe it is our duty to provide
you with as safe a workplace as we possibly can. For your protection, we
have an in-house safety inspection program and we enlist the services of
outside safety consulting firms. We also have a substance abuse policy,
because you have a right to know you can depend on your co-workers.
The only things we require for employment, compensation. Advancement
and benefits are performance & a good team attitude; however, all
employment at our office is Flat will.' No one will be denied opportunities
or benefits on the basis of age, sex, color, race, creed, national origin.
Religious persuasion, marital status, political belief, or disability that does
not prohibit performance of essential job does not function; nor will anyone
receive special treatment for those reasons.
Purpose OF This Manual
This Manual has been prepared to inform you about our offices history,
philosophy, employment practices, and policies, as well as the benefits
provided to you as a valued employee and the conduct expected from you.
No employee manual can answer every question, nor would we want to
restrict the normal question and answer interchange among us. It is in our
person-to-person conversations that we can better know each other, express
our views, and work together in a harmonious relationship.

title: About our office
text:
About our office
The mission of Smile Studio Dentistry is to be profitable providing high
quality, ethical dentistry with a small and highly motivated team.
What you can expect from our office
Smile Studio Dentistry established employee relations policy is to:
Operate an economically successful business so that a consistent level of
steady work is available.
1. Select people on the basis of skill, training, ability, attitude, and character
without discrimination with regard to age, sex, color, race, creed, national
origin, religious persuasion, marital status, political belief, or disability that
does not prohibit performance of essential job functions.
2. Pay all employees according to their effort and contribution to the success
of our business.
4. Review wages, employee benefits and working conditions constantly with
the objective of providing maximum benefits in these areas, consistent with
sound business practices.
5. Provide paid vacations and holidays to all eligible employees.
6. Dedicate ourselves to quality, caring dentistry in an atmosphere of
"fun" and change.
7. Develop competent people who understand and meet our objectives,
and who accept with open minds the ideas, suggestions and constructive
criticisms of fellow employees

title: Employment Classifications
text:
Employment Classifications
At the time you are hired, you are classified as full-time, part-time or
temporary. Unless otherwise specified, the benefits described in this Manual
apply only to full-time employees. All other policies described in this
Manual and communicated by our office apply to all employees, with the
exception of certain wage, salary. If you are unsure of which job
classification your position fits into, please ask your manager.
Full-Time Employees
An employee who has successfully completed the Introductory Period (of a
3 month trial period) of employment and who works at least forty (40) hours
per week is considered a full-time employee.
If you were a full-time employee and have been on an approved leave of
absence, upon return you will be considered a full-time employee, provided
you return to work as agreed in the provisions of your leave.
Part-Time Employees
An employee who works less than a regular forty (40) hour workweek is
considered a part-time employee, if you are a part-time employee; please
understand that you are not eligible for benefits described in this Manual,
except as granted on occasion, or to the extent required by provision of state
and federal laws.
Temporary Employees
From time to time, our office may hire employees for specific periods of
time or for the completion of a specific project. Art employee hired under
these conditions will be considered a temporary employee. The job
assignment, work schedule and duration of the position will be determined
on an individual basis.

title: ATTENDANCE AND PUNCTUALITY
text:
ATTENDANCE AND PUNCTUALITY
All employees should report to work on time, adhering to work the hours
assigned to him/her. If an employee is unable to work for any reason, he/she
should contact his/her supervisor as soon as possible so alternate
arrangements can be made.
Supervisors will keep records of attendance and tardiness. Problem
situations will be brought to an employee's attention and immediate
improvement will be expected. Repeated tardiness or absenteeism may be
grounds for disciplinary action up to and including termination. Employees
must speak directly to their supervisor to report an absence or tardiness.
Messages left on voice mail are not considered acceptable reporting.
Morning Huddles
Morning huddles are a must in the office. Each employee must sign in on the
Morning huddle check sheet list each morning. If they do not due so because
they missed it or because they were late, the employee will be penalized. It
is extremely important that you attend because here is where the office gets
ready for the day, without any surprises.
Keep in mind that the use of the telephone for personal purposes should be
kept to a minimum the use of cellular phones at office hours and Internet use
such as chatting or navigating for personal purposes is completely
prohibited. Photocopy machines and the mailing system are to be used for
Company business only.

title: Customer Relations
text:
Customer Relations
The success of our office depends upon the quality of the relationships
between our office, our employees, our patients, our suppliers and the
general public. Our patients' impression of our office and their interest and
willingness to purchase from us is greatly formed by the people who serve
them. In a sense, regardless of your position, you are our office's
ambassador. The more goodwill you promote, the more our patients will
respect and appreciate you, our office and our office's products and services.
Here are several things you can do to help give customers a good impression
of our office:
1.
Act competently and deal with customers in a courteous and
respectful manner.
2. Communicate pleasantly and respectfully with other employees at all
times.
3. Follow up on orders and questions promptly, provide businesslike replies
to inquiries and requests, and perform all duties loan orderly manner.
4. Take great pride in your work and enjoy doing your very best.
These are the building blocks for your and our office's continued success.
Thank you for adding your support

observed. This is reflected in all our office practices and policies regarding
hiring, training, promotions, transfers, rates of pay, layoff, and other forms
of compensation. All matters relating to employment are based upon ability
to perform the job, as well as dependability and reliability once hired.

title: Harassment
text:
Harassment
Our office intends to provide a work environment that is pleasant, healthful,
comfortable, and free from intimidation, hostility or other offenses which
might interfere with work performance. Harassment of any sort; verbal,
physical, visual will not be tolerated.
What Is Harassment?
Harassment can take many forms. It may be, but is not limited to: words,
signs, jokes, pranks, intimidation, physical contact, or violence. Harassment
is not necessarily sexual in nature.
Sexual harassment may include unwelcome sexual advances, requests for
sexual favors, other verbal or physical contact of a sexual nature when such
conduct creates an intimidating environment, prevents an individual from
effectively performing the duties of their position, or when such conduct is
made a condition of employment or compensation, either implicit or
explicitly.
Responsibility
As an office employee, you are responsible for keeping our work
environment free of harassment Any employee, who becomes aware of an
incident of harassment, whether by witnessing the incident or being told of
it, must report it to Dr. Gonzalez or to Carol Gonzalez, When our office
becomes aware that harassment might exist, it is obligated by law to take
prompt and appropriate action, whether or not the victim wants the company
to do so.
Reporting
If you feel that you have experienced harassment, report the incident
immediately to Dr. Gonzalez or to Carol Gonzalez. Appropriate
investigation and disciplinary action will be taken. All reports will be
promptly investigated with due regard for the privacy of everyone involved.
Any employee found to have harassed a fellow employee or subordinate will

signs, jokes, pranks, intimidation, physical contact, or violence. Harassment
is not necessarily sexual in nature.
Sexual harassment may include unwelcome sexual advances, requests for
sexual favors, other verbal or physical contact of a sexual nature when such
conduct creates an intimidating environment, prevents an individual from
effectively performing the duties of their position, or when such conduct is
made a condition of employment or compensation, either implicit or
explicitly.
Responsibility
As an office employee, you are responsible for keeping our work
environment free of harassment Any employee, who becomes aware of an
incident of harassment, whether by witnessing the incident or being told of
it, must report it to Dr. Gonzalez or to Carol Gonzalez, When our office
becomes aware that harassment might exist, it is obligated by law to take
prompt and appropriate action, whether or not the victim wants the company
to do so.
Reporting
If you feel that you have experienced harassment, report the incident
immediately to Dr. Gonzalez or to Carol Gonzalez. Appropriate
investigation and disciplinary action will be taken. All reports will be
promptly investigated with due regard for the privacy of everyone involved.

title: Introductory Period
text:
Introductory Period
Your first ninety (90) days of employment at our office are considered an
Introductory Period, and during that period you will not accrue benefits
described in this Manual unless otherwise required by law. This Introductory
Period will be a tune for getting to know your fellow employees, Dr.
Gonzalez and the tasks involved in your job position, as well as becoming
familiar with our offices products and services. Dr. Gonzalez will work
closely with you to help you understand the needs and processes of your job.
This Introductory period is a try-out time for both you, as an employee, and
our office, as an employer. During this Introductory Period, our office will
evaluate your suitability for employment and you can evaluate our office as
well at any tin during this first ninety (90) days, you may resign without any
detriment to your record. If, during this period, your work habits, attitude,
attendance or performance does not measure up to our standards, we may
release you. If you take approved time off in excess of five workdays during
the Introductory Period, the Introductory Period may be extended by that
length of time.
At the end of the Introductory Period, Dr. Gonzalez will discuss your job
performance with you. This review will be much the same as the normal job
performance review that is held for regular full-time or part employees on a
semi-annual basis. During the course of the discussion, you are encouraged
to give your comments and ideas as well.
Please understand that completion of the introductory period does not
guarantee continued employment for any specified period of time, nor does
it require that an employee be discharged only for "cause"
A former employee who has been rehired after a separation from our office
of more than one (1) year is considered an introductory employee during
their first ninety (90) days following rehire.
Knowledge of our Office
After having learned to competently perform your own duties, your next step
is to familiarize yourself with our office activities. This can prove valuable
to you, our customers and our office as well. Our office may provide
additional "cross-training"

title: Standards of Conduct
text:
Standards of Conduct
Whenever people gather together to achieve goals, some rules of conduct are
needed to help everyone work together efficiently, effectively, and
harmoniously. Some people have problems with "rules" and 'authority
figures," and past experience may have justified these thoughts and feelings;
however, at our office, we hold ourselves to a high standard of quality where
the rules and authority figures simply assure that quality is maintained.
By accepting employment with us, you have a responsibility to our office
and to your fellow employees to adhere to certain rules of behavior and
conduct The purpose of these rules is not to restrict your rights, but rather to
be certain that you understand what conduct is expected and necessary.
When each person is aware that he or she can fully depend upon fellow
workers to follow the rules of conduct, then our organization will be a better
place to work for everyone.
Unacceptable Activities
Generally speaking, we expect each person to act in a mature and
responsible way at all times. However, to avoid any possible confusion,
some of the more obvious unacceptable activities are noted below. Your
avoidance of these activities will be to your benefit as well as the benefit of
our office. If you have any questions concerning any work or safety rule, or
any of the unacceptable activities listed, please see your manager for an
explanation.
Occurrences of any of the following violations, because of their seriousness,
may result in immediate dismissal without warning
* Willful violation of any company rule; any deliberate action that is
extreme in nature and is obviously detrimental to our office's efforts to
operate profitably.

title: Employment Policies
text:
Employment Policies
Whether you are a new hire or a former employee returning to our office, you may feel a
little strange in your new surroundings. This is a normal feeling and is expected. Your
fellow employees, especially Dr. Gonzalez, want to help you get off to a good start. Feel
free to ask for help concerning anything you don't understand
One of the first things you should do is carefully read this Manual. It is designed to
answer many of your questions about the practices and policies of our office, what you
can expect from our office, and what our office expects from you.
Anniversary Date
The first day you report to work is your "official anniversary date. Your anniversary date
is used to compute various conditions and benefits described in this Manual.
Licensure and Certification
Dental hygienists are required to display their current license to practice dental hygiene in
their operatory. A current dental hygiene license is a requirement for employment.
All employees are required to have a current CPR- emergency education certificate from
the American Red Cross. All dental assistants are required to be certified to take X-rays.
Certification is a condition for employment by Dr.Gonzalez.
At Will Employment
All employment and compensation with Smile Studio Dentistry is "at will" in that they
can be terminated with or without cause, and with or without notice, at any time, at the
option of either Dr. Gonzalez or yourself, except as otherwise provided by law.

free to ask for help concerning anything you don't understand
One of the first things you should do is carefully read this Manual. It is designed to
answer many of your questions about the practices and policies of our office, what you
can expect from our office, and what our office expects from you.
Anniversary Date
The first day you report to work is your "official anniversary date. Your anniversary date
is used to compute various conditions and benefits described in this Manual.
Licensure and Certification
Dental hygienists are required to display their current license to practice dental hygiene in
their operatory. A current dental hygiene license is a requirement for employment.
All employees are required to have a current CPR- emergency education certificate from

At Will Employment
All employment and compensation with Smile Studio Dentistry is "at will" in that they
can be terminated with or without cause, and with or without notice, at any time, at the
option of either Dr. Gonzalez or yourself, except as otherwise provided by law.

title: Your particular hours of work and the scheduling of your lunch period will be…
text:
Your particular hours of work and the scheduling of your lunch period will be determined
and assigned by Dr. Gonzalez. Most employees are assigned to work a forty (40) hour
work week. You are required to take a one (1) hour unpaid lunch period daily; please
understand that you may not "work through lunch" in order to arrive late or to leave early
or to work extra time-At our office we try and answer the phone through the official
lunch time of one to two. Thus, one employee will take his/her lunch break before or after
the official lunch hour.
Confidential Information
Our patients entrust our office with important information relating to their health and life.
The nature of this relationship requires maintenance of confidentiality. In safeguarding
the information received, our office earns the respect and further trust of our patients.
Your employment with our office assumes an obligation to maintain confidentiality, even
after you leave our employ. Any violation of confidentiality seriously injures our office's
reputation and effectiveness. Therefore, please do not discuss our office business with
anyone who does not work for us, and never discuss business transactions with anyone
who does not have a direct association with the transaction. Even casual remarks can be
misinterpreted and repeated, so develop the personal discipline necessary to maintain
confidentiality. If you hear, see or become aware of anyone else breaking this trust,
consider what they might do with information they get from you.
If you are questioned by someone outside the office and you are concerned about the
appropriateness of giving them certain information, remember that you are not required
to answer, and that we do not wish you do. Instead, as politely as possible, refer the
request to Dr. Gonzalez.
No one is permitted to remove or make copies of office records, reports or documents
without prior management approval.
Because of its seriousness, disclosure of confidential information will lead to dismissal.

title: Wage & Salary Policies
text:
Wage & Salary Policies
Our office has developed policies to insure wages and salaries
comparable to those of other employees with similar jobs at our
office or in our industry. Our wage and salary policy is designed to
attract and retain the best-qualified people available.
To carry out this policy, we periodically compare our wage and
salary policy with community rates for similar positions using
appropriate published information from sources like statewide
business organizations, local chambers of commerce, state and
national organizations, various management reports, and various
local, state and federal agencies.
Deductions from Paycheck (Mandatory)
Our office is required by law to make certain deductions from your
paycheck each time one is prepared. Among these are your federal,
state and local income taxes and your contribution to Social
Security as required by law. These deductions will be itemized on
your check stub. The amount of the deductions may depend on
your earnings and on the information you furnish on your W-4
form regarding the number of dependents/exemptions you claim.
Any change in name, address, telephone number, marital status or
number of exemptions must be reported to the Office Manager
immediately, to ensure proper credit for tax purposes. The W-2
form you receive for each year indicates precisely how much of
your earnings were deducted for these purposes.
Any other mandatory deductions to be made from your paycheck,
such as court-ordered attachments, will be explained whenever our
office is ordered to make such deductions. Some states may require
other payroll deductions.

Docking From Wages
The wages of any 'non-exempt employee who is tardy for work
will be "docked" for the time not worked. Three incidents of
lateness during a 90-day period will be considered a "tardiness
pattern' and will result in disciplinary action in addition to the
"docking' of pay. A record of all lateness and absenteeism is
maintained in your personnel file.
Error in Pay
Every effort is made to avoid errors in your paycheck. If you
believe an error has been made, tell your manager immediately. He
or she will take the necessary steps to research the problem and to
assure that any necessary correction is made properly and
promptly.

title: COMPENSATION
text:
COMPENSATION
Smile Studio Dentistry is committed to maintaining competitive salaries.
PAYMENT METHOD/WORK WEEK
All employees are paid Bi-weekly for duties performed in those two weeks.
The workweek is defined as beginning at 12:01 am on Sunday and ending at
midnight on Sunday.
To complete the payroll and prepare paychecks, you must turn your time
sheets in to the office every day.
You are urged to review your paycheck carefully for written errors, if you
find a mistake, report it to your manager immediately who will take the
necessary steps in making any paycheck adjustments. Your checks will be
administered and delivered thru "Paychexs" directly. Payments are made on
the 15t and the 30*h of each month.
JOB PERFORMANCE

title: Performance & Compensation Reviews
text:
Performance & Compensation Reviews
Performance Reviews
Your manager is continuously evaluating your job performance. Day-to-day interaction
between you and your manager should give you a sense of how your manager perceives
your performance.
However, to avoid haphazard or incomplete evaluations, our office conducts a formal
review once a year for each employee.
Performance reviews will be conducted annually on or about each employee's
anniversary date. New employees may be reviewed more frequently. A review may also
be conducted in the event of a promotion or change in duties and responsibilities.
During formal performance reviews, your manager will consider the following things,
among others:
I
2
3
4
5
Attendance, initiative and effort
Knowledge of your work
Attitude and willingness
The quality and quantity of your work
The conditions under which you work
The primary reason for performance reviews is to identify your strengths and weaknesses
in order to reinforce your good habits and develop ways to improve in your weaker areas.
This review also serves to make you aware of and to document how your job
performance compares to the goals and description of your job. This is a good time to
discuss your interests and future goals. Your manager is interested in helping you to
progress and grow in order to achieve personal as well as work-related goals D perhaps
he or she can recommend further training or additional opportunities for you.
In addition to individual job performance reviews, our office periodically conducts a
review of job descriptions to insure that we are fully aware of any changes in the duties
and responsibilities of each position and those changes are recognized and adequately
compensated.

living.

title: Termination & Severance Pay
text:
Termination & Severance Pay
Our office does not pay severance pay. When you leave our office, you will
be paid for actual time worked.
Time Cards/ Records
You must record on the time sheet the days you work or are absent due to
illness, vacation, Jury duty, etc.
Hourly Employees
By law, we are obligated to keep accurate records of the time worked" This
is done by the honor system. Since Dr. Gonzalez, trust all employees to
write down on their time sheet, their time of arrival and departure.
You are responsible for your time card. No one may record hours worked on
another's card. Tampering with another's time card is cause for disciplinary
action, including possible dismissal of both employees. Do not alter another
person's record, or influence anyone else to alter your record for you. In the
event of an error in recording your time, report the matter to Dr. Gonzalez
immediately.
Wage Assignments (Garnishments)
We hope you will manage your financial affairs so that we will not be
obligated to execute any court-ordered wage assignment or garnishment
against your wages. However, whenever court- ordered deductions are to be
taken from your paycheck, you will be notified. According to the Federal
Wage Garnishment Act, three (3) or more garnishments may be cause for
dismissal.

title: Work Schedule
text:
Work Schedule
The normal workweek consists of five (5) Monday through Friday (for some
employees). Your schedule of daily work hours will be given to you by Dr.
Gonzalez. You will be notified promptly whenever a change is necessary.
Should you have any questions concerning your work schedule, please ask
Dr. Gonzalez.
Absence or lateness
From time to time, it may be necessary for you to be absent from work. Our
office is aware that emergencies, illnesses, or pressing personal business that
cannot be scheduled outside your work hours may arise. Sick days and
personal days have been provided for this purpose.
If you are unable to report to work, or if you will arrive late, please contact
Dr. Gonzalez or Carol Gonzalez immediately. Give him or her as much time
as possible to arrange for someone else to cover your position until you
arrive. If you know in advance that you will need to be absent, you are
required to request this time off directly from your manager He or she will
determine when will be the most suitable time for you to be absent from
your work.
Absence from work for three (3) consecutive days without notifying your
manager or the personnel administrator will be considered a voluntary
resignation.
Attendance
You are expected to be at your work station and ready to work at the
beginning of your assigned daily work hours, and you are expected to
remain at your work station until the end of your assigned work hours,
except for approved breaks and lunch. When your work takes you away
from your work station, please let your manager know where you are going
and how long you expect to be gone.
Be aware that 'excessive" time off could lead to disciplinary action.

come under question. Tardiness or leaving early is as detrimental to our

considered a "tardiness patter" and will carry the same weight as an

disciplinary action, including possible dismissal.

return to work on time at the end of your lunch period.

title: The Benefits Package
text:
The Benefits Package
In addition to receiving an equitable salary and having an equal opportunity
for professional development and advancement, you may be eligible to enjoy
other benefits which will enhance your job satisfaction. We are certain that
you will agree that the benefits program described in this Manual represents
a very large investment by our office, and we trust that you will avoid
abusing any of the program's benefits.
A good benefits program is a solid investment in our office and its
employees. It not only insures the loyalty of long-time capable employees, it
also helps to attract talented newcomers who can help our office grow. Our
office will periodically review the benefits program and will make
modifications as appropriate to the company's condition.
Eligibility for Benefits
If you are a full-time employee, you will enjoy all of the benefits described
in this manual as soon as you meet the eligibility requirements for each
particular benefit.
If you are a part-time employee, you will or only those benefits which are
required by law to be afforded to you, provided that you meet the minimum
requirements set forth by law and in the benefit plans).
No benefits are available to you during your Introductory Period, except as
otherwise provided by law.
Temporary employees are not eligible for benefits.
Paid Leaves of Absence
Time off for any reason during a working day will count first against your
allotted sick days or personal days, as appropriate, in hourly, quarter day,
half day or full day increments, Once you have used all of your earned sick
or personal days, the time will be counted against your earned vacation time.
Thereafter, unless specifically accepted, any time off will be without pay.

title: Other Paid Leaves
text:
Other Paid Leaves
Jury Duty
It is your civic duty as a citizen to report for jury duty whenever called If
you are called for jury duty, we will permit you to take the necessary time
off and we wish to help you avoid any financial loss because of such service.
If you have completed your Introductory Period, our office will reimburse
you for the difference between your jury pay and your regular pay, not to
exceed eight (8) hours per day, for a maximum of two (2) business days.
You must notify your manager within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt of the
jury summons.
On any day or half-day you are not required to serve, you will be expected to
return to work. In order to receive jury duty pay, you must present a
statement of jury service and pay to your manager. This document is issued
by the court.
Sick Leave
In order to provide full time staff a measure of financial protection in the
event of a short term illness Smile Studio Dentistry staff earn 3 sick days per
year, that must be utilized.
If you have not been employed for a full year with our office, you will be
eligible for paid sick days upon completion of your Introductory Period (90
days)

title: Unpaid Leaves of Absence
text:
Unpaid Leaves of Absence
Occasionally, for medical, personal, or other reasons, you may need to be
temporarily released from the duties of your job with our office, but may not
wish to submit your resignation. Under certain circumstances, you may be
eligible for an unpaid leave of absence. An unpaid leave of absence may be
granted for a minimum of thirty (8) days.
You must apply in writing for an unpaid leave of absence, setting forth the
reason for the leave, the date on which you wish the leave to begin and the
date on which you wilt return to active employment with our office. Submit
your application to your manager, who will bring your request before the
appropriate members of management for approval.
A leave will be granted only when operating conditions at our office permit.
The needs of our office will determine the number of employees allowed out
on unpaid leave at anyone time.
You must adhere to all the requirements set forth in the following sections.
Failure to do so may result in alterations of your employment status or
termination of your employment with our office.
Disability (Including Pregnancy) Leave Of Absence
Our office may grant an unpaid leave of absence for illness, disability or
pregnancy. To request a disability leave of absence from your manager, you
should submit, or have someone submit for you, a statement of ill health or
disability from your doctor. (Pregnancy is treated, for the purposes of policy,
the same as an illness or disability.) An approved disability leave may be
granted for up to ninety (90) days. If necessary, you may request extensions
in thirty (30) day increments for a maximum of six ((6) months. Whenever
possible, you are required to give as much notice as possible of your pending
need for a disability leave of absence.
In the case of pregnancy, please inform your manager as soon as possible of
the date you and your doctor anticipate that you will begin your leave. Your

Workers' Compensation
The Texas Workers' Compensation Law is a no-fault insurance plan which
is supervised by the state and one hundred percent (100%) paid for by our
office. This law was designed to provide you with benefits for any injury
which you may suffer in connection with your employment. Under the
provisions of the law, if you are injured while at work, you are eligible to
apply for Workers Compensation.
What Is Workers' Compensation?
Texas no-fault Worker& Compensation law was passed by the State
legislature to guarantee prompt, automatic benefits to workers injured on the
job.
Before Workers Compensation an injured worker had to sue his employer to
recover medical costs and lost wages. Lawsuits took months and sometimes
years. Juries and judges had to decide who was at fault and how much, if
anything, would be paid. In most cases, the injured worker got nothing. It
was a costly, time-consuming and unfair system.
Today, if you're unable to work because of a job injury, our office and our
Workers' Compensation Insurance carrier work together to take care of your
medical expenses and pay you money to live on until you're able to come
back to work automatically, without delay or red tape.
Who Is Covered?
Every our office employee is protected by Worker& Compensation.
What Is Covered?
Any injury is covered if it's caused by your job, not just serious accidents,

title: statements regarding the on-the-job accident so that we may accurately
text:
statements regarding the on-the-job accident so that we may accurately
document the incident and so you may receive all the benefits to which you
are entitled. (Failure to do this could result in loss of benefits.)
Unemployment Compensation
Our office pays a percentage of its payroll to the Unemployment
Compensation Fund according to our office's employment history. If you
become unemployed, you may be eligible for unemployment compensation,
under certain conditions, for a limited period of time. Unemployment
compensation provides temporary Income for workers who have lost their
jobs. To be eligible you must have earned a certain amount and be willing
and able to work. You should apply for benefits through your local State
Unemployment Office as soon as possible.
Social Security
The United States Government operates a system of contributory insurance
known as Social Security. As a wage earner, you are required by law to
contribute a set amount of your weekly wages to the trust fluid from which
benefits are paid. As your employer, our office is required to deduct this
amount from each paycheck you receive. In addition, our office matches
your contribution dollar for dollar, thereby paying one-half of the cost of
your Social Security benefits.

text:
Bulletin Boards
Bulletins and bulletin board(s) are our 'official" way of keeping everyone
informed about new policies, changes in procedures and special event.
Information of general interest is posted regularly on the bulletin board(s).
Please form the habit of reading the bulletin board(s) regularly so that you

Only authorized personnel are permitted to post, remove or alter any notice

bulletin boards), see your manager for instructions
Communications
Successful working conditions and relationships depend upon successful
communication. Not only do you need to stay aware of changes in
procedures, policies and general information, you also need to communicate
your ideas suggestions, personal goals or problems as they affect your work.
In addition to the exchanges of Information and expressions of ideas and
attitudes which occur daily, make certain you are aware of and utilize all our
office methods of communication, including this Employee Manual, bulletin
boards, discussions with your manager, memoranda, staff meetings,
newsletters, training sessions, etc.
Company Meetings
On occasion, we may request that you attend a company sponsored meeting
If this is scheduled during your regular working hours, your attendance is
required. If it is held during your non- working hours and you decide to
attend, you will be paid for the time you spend traveling to and from the
meeting as well as for time spent at the meeting.

title: Computer Software (Unauthorized Copying)
text:
Computer Software (Unauthorized Copying)
Our office does not condone the illegal duplication of software. The
copyright law is clear. The copyright holder is given certain exclusive rights,
including the right to make and distribute copies. Title 17 of the U.S. Code
states that 'it is illegal to make or distribute copies of copyrighted material
without authorization" (Section 106). The only exception is the users' right
to make a backup copy for archival purposes (Section 117).
The law protects the exclusive rights of the copyright holder and does not
give users the right to copy software unless a backup copy is not provided by
the manufacturer. Unauthorized duplication of software is a Federal crime.
Penalties include fines of as much as $100,000 and jail terms of up to five
years.
Even the users of unlawful copies suffer from their own illegal actions. They
receive no documentation, no customer support and no information about
product updates.
1. Our office licenses the use of computer software from a variety of outside
companies. Our office does not own this software or its related
documentation and, unless authorized by the software manufacturer, does
not have the right to reproduce it.
2. With regard to use on local area networks or on multiple machines, our
office employees shall use the software only in accordance with the license
agreement.
3. Our office employees learning of any misuse of software or related
documentation within the company shall notify the department manager or
our office legal counsel.
4. According to the U.S. Copyright Law, illegal reproduction of software can
be subject to civil damages and criminal penalties, including fines and
imprisonment, our office employees who make acquire or use unauthorized
copies of computer software shall be disciplined as appropriate under the
circumstances. Such discipline may include dismissal.

title: First Aid
text:
First Aid
Federal law (FOSI requires that we keep records of all illnesses and
accidents which occur during the workday. The Texas state Workers
Compensation Act also requires that you report any illness or injury on the
job, no matter how slight. If you hurt yourself or become ill, please contact
your manager for assistance. If you fail to report an injury, you may
jeopardize your right to collect workers compensation payments as well as
health benefits. OSHA also provides for your right to know about any health
hazards which might be present on the job. Should you have any questions
or concerns, contact Dr. Gonzalez.

title: 1. See Your Manager First.
text:
1. See Your Manager First.
If there is anything bothering you, or if you have a suggestion, we would
like to hear about it. If you feel that any working condition, policy, practice,
or action by our office or by any member of management is unjust, you
should tell your manager about it and discuss the matter confidentially and
in private with him or her. If you decide to do this, please stay in your
workplace and contact your manager, or one of the other managers that may
have been designated for you to contact, before leaving. Establish with your
manager an appropriate time and place to discuss your concern. If for some
reason your manager fails to offer you the opportunity to discuss the matter,
or if the discussion does not lead to a satisfactory conclusion, then proceed
to the next step.
2. Put It In Writing.
It makes a difference when you put your grievance/suggestion in writing
understanding the situation and what you think the ideal condition should be,
as well as some ideas for achieving your desired condition, will help your
manager go to work for you. Ask your manager for a 'Bright Idea" form to
assist you with presenting your complaint or proposed solution to a problem
or situation. Explain the present situation, the desired condition, and your
proposed solution/suggestion. Submit this completed form to your manager.
If, after discussion with your manager, the situation remains unsettled, the
matter should be referred to senior management. You may need to elaborate
your complaint or See Your Manager proposed solution

title: Your manager is in complete charge of the department. He or she is
text:
Your manager is in complete charge of the department. He or she is
responsible for the efficient operation of the department. Your manager has
authority to hire and dismiss, to assign work, recommend pay increases,
transfers or promotions, and to maintain
order and discipline. This may be
accomplished by the manager personally.
Your manager is human, has many responsibilities, and needs your
cooperation, assistance, and loyalty. He wants to help you that are their job,
so please ask, and please be willing to meet him half way-if he cannot help
you or answer your question, your question will be referred to someone who
can. You can expect to be treated fairly and with respect. Smile Studio
Dentistry, has a direct interest in you. We want you to consider us as your
advisor, friend and mentor. Go to your Dr. Gonzalez for information about
your job, your pay, or other matters of company policy.
Outside Activities
No employee may take an outside job, either for pay or as a donation of his
or her personal time, with a customer or competitor of our office; nor may
they do work on their own if it competes in any way with the sales of
products or services we provide our customers. If your financial situation
requires you to hold a second job, part-time or full-time, or if you intend to
engage in a business enterprise of your own, we would like to know about it.
Before accepting any outside employment it would be a good idea to discuss
the matter with your Dr. Gonzalez.
Parking Lot
You are encouraged to use the back parking areas designated for our
employees. Please keep in mind that the parking spaces adjacent to or in
front of our building(s) are for customers and visitors only. Remember to
lock your car every day and park within the specified areas.
Courtesy and common sense in parking will avoid accidents, personal
injuries, and damage to your vehicle and to the vehicles of other employees.
If you should damage another car while parking or leaving, immediately
report the incident, along with the license numbers of both vehicles and any
other pertinent information you may have, to your manager.

textEs:

Actividades externas
Ningún empleado podrá aceptar un trabajo externo, ya sea a cambio de una remuneración o como donación de su parte.

title: Property & Equipment Care
text:
Property & Equipment Care
It is your responsibility to understand the machines you need to use to
perform your duties. Good care of any machine that you use during the
course of your employment, as well as the conservative use of supplies, will
benefit you and our office, If you find that a machine is not working
properly or in any way appears unsafe, please notify your manager
immediately so that repairs or adjustment may be made. Under no
circumstances should you start or operate a machine you deem unsafe, nor
should you adjust or modify the safeguards provided.
Recycling, Waste Prevention & Conservation
Our office actively recycles as many materials as possible:
Waste of time, materials, equipment and utilities is costly to you and our
office. You can help make every minute count. Eliminate waste whenever
possible. In the long rim, you will benefit by helping to reduce operating
costs. The money saved by eliminating waste can be passed along to
employees In the form of profit-based bonuses and other benefits.
Resignation
While we hope both you and our office will mutually benefit from your
continued employment, we realize that it become necessary for you to leave
your job with our office. If you anticipate having to resign your position
with our office, you are expected to notify your manager at least two (2)
weeks In advance of the date that you must leave.
Safety Rules
Safety is everybody's business. Safety is to be given primary importance in
every aspect of planning and performing all our office activities. We want to
protect you against industrial injury and illness, as well as minimize the
potential loss of production.

text:

title: • Walk do not run.
text:
• Walk do not run.
• Use stairs one at a time.
• Report to your manager if you or a co-worker becomes ill or is
injured.
• Ask for assistance when lifting heavy objects or moving heavy
furniture.
• Keep cabinet doors and file and desk drawers closed when not in use.
• Never empty any trash tray into a waste basket or open receptacle.
• Sit firmly and squarely in chairs that roll or tilt.
• Wear or use appropriate safety equipment as required in your work.
• Avoid 'horseplay" or practical jokes.
• Start work on any machine only after safety procedures and
requirements have been explained and you understand them.
• Use air hoses only for the use intended. Avoid blowing air at yourself
or anyone else.
• Wear appropriate personal protective equipment, like shoes, hats,
gloves, goggles, spats, hearing protectors, etc., in designated areas or
when working on an operation which requires their use.
• Keep your work area clean and orderly, and the aisles clear.
• Stack materials only to safe heights.
• Watch out for the safety of fellow employees.
• Wear gloves whenever handling castings, scrap, barrels, etc.
• Operate motorized equipment only if authorized by your immediate
manager. ALL operators must be licensed by our office.
• Remember failure to adhere to these rules will be considered serious
infractions of safety rules and will result in disciplinary actions.
Security

title: Maintaining the security of our office buildings and vehicles is every
text:
Maintaining the security of our office buildings and vehicles is every
employee's responsibility. Develop habits that insure security as a matter of
course. For example:
Always keep cash properly secured. If you are aware that cash is insecurely
stored, immediately inform the person responsible.
Know the location of all alarms and fire extinguishers, and familiarize
yourself with the proper procedure for using them, should the need arise;
When you leave our office's premises make sure that all entrances are
properly locked and secured.
Smoking
Please don't smoke in areas where you are directly serving customers and
where it may be offensive to your co-workers. If you smoke, there are a
variety of places appropriate for you to enjoy a short break outside the
practice. Please be courteous and concerned about the needs of your fellow
employees and others. The wishes and preferences of non-smokers will take
precedence over those of employees who smoke. Smoking is permitted in
private offices if the occupant allows it. Please do not smoke in restricted
areas.
Solicitations & Distributions
Solicitation for any cause during working time and in working areas is not
permitted. You are not permitted to distribute non-company literature in
work areas at any time during working time.

title: Working time is defined as the time assigned for the performance of your
text:
Working time is defined as the time assigned for the performance of your
job and does not apply to break periods and meal times. Working areas do
not include the lunch room or the parking areas. Solicitation during
authorized meal and break periods is permitted so long as it is not conducted
in working areas. However, employees are not permitted to sell chances,
merchandise or otherwise solicit money or contributions without
management approval.
Persons not employed by our office are prohibited from soliciting or
distributing literature on company property.
Substance Abuse
Our office is committed to providing its employees with a safe workplace
and an atmosphere which allows them to protect inventory and other assets
placed in their care; our office employees should not be subject to any safety
threats from fellow workers. You are expected to be in suitable mental and
physical condition while at work, allowing you to perform your job
effectively and safely.
Whenever use or abuse of any mood altering substance (such as alcohol or
other drugs) interferes with a safe workplace, appropriate action must be
taken, our office has no desire to intrude into its employee's personal lives.
However, both on-the-job and off-the-job involvement with any mood
altering substances can have an impact on our workplace and on our office's
ability to achieve its objectives of safety and security. Therefore, you are
expected to report to the workplace with no mood altering substances in
your body. While you may make your own lifestyle choices our office
cannot accept the risk in the workplace which substance use or abuse may
create. The possession, sale or use of mood altering substances at the
workplace, or coming to work wider the influence of such substances shall
be a violation of safe work practices and will be subject to disciplinary
action, including possible dismissal.

Property theft of any type will not be tolerated by our office. We consider

immediate family. Under no circumstances should company products be

Employees are permitted to buy company products at a discount for persona

Our office considers such behavior a form of theft and violators will be

4. Taking of company property. No item purchased or supplied by our office
should ever be removed from company premises without express
authorization of your immediate manager and the proper paper work
associated with the situation. This rule applies to all company property
including raw materials used in manufacturing plants, mechanics, tools,
computers, and even pens and paper. All employees may be subject to
random searches as they leave company facilities. Your manager has been
given detailed instructions on the circumstances in which he or she can
authorize you to borrow company equipment or to take samples of your
work home. A checkout procedure will be used, and if you fail to return any
item removed on schedule, the value of the items will be charged against
your paycheck and you may be subject to disciplinary action for theft.
Penalty Clause
Unauthorized possession or removal of company property is a very serious
offense. Employees violating this policy will be subjected to discipline up to
and including possible dismissal and prosecution. Our office will consider
the dollar value of the items) taken, the employee's seniority, and the
employees past work record in setting penalties. If you are dismissed
because of unauthorized possession or removal of company property, the
reason for your dismissal will be provided to any future employer that
contacts our office. Referrals to criminal authorities will be made on a case-
by-case basis.

title: CLEANING THE RECEPTION AREA
text:
CLEANING THE RECEPTION AREA
Desired Outcome: The reception area is cleaned and straightened just before the
lunch hour and at the end of each day.
Measurement: Visual inspection of the reception area. Feedback from patients,
the doctor, and all other fellow staff members.
1. After the last morning patient leaves and before the first afternoon patient ar-
rives, clean these items with Windex and paper towels: (Don't forget to wear
gloves!)
A. glass on the front door
B. chair arms
C. reception desk counter top
2. Straighten the reception area.
A. magazines
B. chairs
C. children's books
D. toys
E. decorative wall hangings and signs
3. Inspect the floor for any visible trash. (i.e. paper, dust balls)
A. Pick up any visible items with gloved hands and discard.
B. Sweep daily.
4. Empty the wicker trash basket and insert a clean 5-gallon trash bag.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 at the end of the day.

title: MONITORING PRODUCTION GOALS
text:
MONITORING PRODUCTION GOALS
ALL PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: Daily production goals are monitored and met every day.
Measurement: End of day production matches or exceeds goal. Review of the
daily reports, Morning Huddle agendas, and daily schedules.
1. At the end of each day and after patient charts have been pulled and prepared
for the following day's schedule, gather and review the charts in preparation for
the next day's huddle. Look for the following:
A. Hygiene patients that need restorative work.
B. Restorative patients that need hygiene appointments.
C. Elective treatments (i.e., bleaching, sealants, etc.)
D. Treatment that has been booked in advance that could be done sooner.
E. Other family members that need treatment.
2. If you find any of the above and your scheduled production is lower than your
goal, contact the patient to try to add them/treatment to the schedule for the next
day.
3. Review and contact the patients on the quick call or priority list.
4. Review the schedule and look for any patients that you could move up. If so,
contact the patient.
5. As a last resort, consolidate schedules to free up blocks of time for side work.
6. If you make any change in a patient's appointment date and time, make sure
you make the appropriate documentation in their chart. Refer to the appropriate
corresponding SOPs to make or change appointments.
7. Update the "Week at a Glance" form on the next day's Morning Huddle
agenda to reflect any changes you've made.

SEGUIMIENTO DE METAS DE PRODUCCIÓN
TODO EL PERSONAL
Resultado deseado: Los objetivos de producción diarios se monitorean y se cumplen todos los días.
Medición: La producción al final del día iguala o excede la meta. Revisión de la
informes diarios, agendas de Morning Huddle y horarios diarios.
1. Al final de cada día y después de que se hayan extraído y preparado los historiales de los pacientes.
Para el programa del día siguiente, recopile y revise los gráficos en preparación para
la reunión del día siguiente. Busque lo siguiente:
A. Higiene de pacientes que necesitan trabajos de restauración.
B. Pacientes restauradores que necesitan citas de higiene.
C. Tratamientos electivos (es decir, blanqueamiento, selladores, etc.)
D. Tratamiento que se haya reservado con antelación y que se pueda realizar antes.
E. Otros familiares que necesitan tratamiento.
2. Si encuentra algo de lo anterior y su producción programada es inferior a su
objetivo, comuníquese con el paciente para intentar agregarlo/tratamiento al cronograma para el próximo
día.
3. Revisar y contactar a los pacientes en la llamada rápida o lista de prioridades.
4. Revise el cronograma y busque pacientes a los que pueda ascender. Si es así,
contactar al paciente.
5. Como último recurso, consolide los horarios para liberar bloques de tiempo para trabajos paralelos.
6. Si realiza algún cambio en la fecha y hora de la cita de un paciente, asegúrese
usted hace la documentación apropiada en su expediente. Consulte el correspondiente
POE correspondientes para realizar o cambiar citas.
7. Actualice el formulario "Resumen de la semana" en la reunión matutina del día siguiente.
agenda para reflejar cualquier cambio que haya realizado.

4. 查看时间表并寻找可以升级的患者。如果是这样的话，

5. 作为最后的手段，整合时间表以腾出大量时间进行副业。

ALL PERSONNEL
Eventually all of us find ourselves on the receiving end of an angry patient's ver-
bal barrage. Those of you that have worked in dental offices for some time know
the kind of patient I'm talking about. If you're new to the field, you'll find out. The
first time it happens you may find yourself completely stuck, not knowing what to
say or how to fix the problem. You will ask yourself, "why is this patient yelling at
me? " After all, you're just doing your job.
As uncomfortable as it may sometimes be, dealing with angry and hostile patients
is part of your job in the dental office. Below are some guidelines that will help
you calm the patient down and empower you to remain in control when faced with
that hostile patient.
Desired Outcome: To calm a hostile patient and diffuse the situation as quickly as
possible, ensure minimal disruption to the office work flow, and reduce individual
stress when faced with conflict of this sort.
Measurement: Successfully calming a hostile patient, feedback from co-workers
and supervisors, and the level of your individual stress at that moment.
1. Introduce yourself. People find it harder to yell and scream at someone they
know.
2. If at all possible, remove the patient from the scene to minimize disruption of
the reception area. Sincerely express to the patient that you understand how
frustrating the situation is, and ask him/or her to accompany you to a treatment
room or the doctor's or office manager's office to discuss the problem and pos-
sible solutions.
3. Sit down. Ask the patient to join you. Body language is an important factor in
determining the type of interaction to occur. By sitting down, you bring the es-
calation level of the communication down a notch. Be controlled, polite, quiet,
secure, and interested. Listen and acknowledge the patient's frustration and an-
ger. Above all, any response you make must be sincere.

ALL

To answer the telephone by the third ring, using a warm,
friendly voice, identifying the office and yourself, and accurately assessing and
meeting the needs of the caller. To accurately complete telephone emergency
slips, message memos, and chart documentation.

phone. Your voice and verbal skills will set the tone for the encounter and ulti-

title: APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: GUIDELINES
text:
APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: GUIDELINES
Insert a copy of an ideal clinic day from your appointment book following this SOP. It will serve as an
easy and complete reference for employees. Include a page that is exactly as it should be! It should be
legible, thorough, and accurate. If none exist, then create a mock schedule based on your ideal clinic day.
Desired Outcome: All appointments are scheduled appropriately and timely according to the patient's
needs and status of appointment schedule.
Measurement: Review of appointment book. Feedback from the doctor, clinical assistants, and patient.
1. Always enter the following information in the appointment book.
Patient's last and first name (i.e., Smith, Mary).
-
If the patient is a child, also enter their parent's or legal guardian's name.
2. If the patient is a disabled adult, also enter their caretaker's or power of attorney's

title: APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: EMERGENCIES
text:
APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: EMERGENCIES
FRONT DESK AND BILLING PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: Emergency patients successfully worked into the schedule
with minimal disruption of other appointments scheduled that day. Also, accurate
and empathetic assessment of the patient's needs.
Measurement: Satisfaction of the emergency patient with minimal delay for
other patients.
1. Determine the necessity and reason for the appointment and pull the chart, if
an established patient.
2. Complete the emergency slip, asking the questions listed on the form and at-
tach it to the patient's chart. Refer to the Forms Section for an Emergency
Telephone Slip.
3. The patient must be seen the same day, if any of the following symptoms ap-
ply:
A. Confirmed trauma. (Refer to the Clinical Evaluation for Trauma form in
the Forms Section.)
B. Pain keeps the patient awake at night.
C. Current fever or swelling.
D. Sudden onset of severe pain.
4. The patient can be seen within the next couple of days, if any of the following
circumstances and symptoms apply:
A. The patient is satisfied with the appointment date and time scheduled.
B. The patient has a history of chronic toothaches that do not keep them
awake at night or require medication.
5. Broken or sensitive tooth causing mild discomfort and the patient is satisfied
with the appointment date and time scheduled.
6. Once an acceptable and appropriate appointment date and time has been se-
lected, enter the following information in the appointment book:
A. Patient's last and first name (i.e., Smith, Mary).
B. Work and home phone numbers.

title: 1099A
text:
1099A
DI VOMIT
APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: X-RAYS
(apptxray.doc)
Desired Outcome: All appointments for diagnostic x-rays are consistently and accurately scheduled.
Patients receive a timely appointment for the necessary x-rays. Patients receive professional and courte-
ous assistance with making the appointment.
Measurement: Review of the appointment book. Feedback from the doctor, assistants, and patients.
Full Mouth X-Rays (FMX)
The doctor usually orders full-mouth x-rays (FMX) on all new patients. The patient's orthodontist or
other specialist(s) can also order full mouth x-rays. The standard FMX includes 4 Bitewings and 14 peri-
apicals. The standard recall protocol for the FMX series is every five years. Although, some insurance
carriers will allow a series every three years.
1. When scheduling full-mouth x-rays:
A. For a new patient, ask whether they have had this series within the last five years.
B. For an established patient, an x-ray history will be documented in their chart.
2. If the patient has insurance, inform them that their insurance may not cover the fee, if:
It is not a benefit under their plan.
The patient has seen an oral surgeon or orthodontist and has had a panorex film
taken.
3. If the patient has had this series within the last 3-5 years, save them from experiencing undue radia-
tion exposure, as well as additional expenses. You or the patient may request these films from the
previous doctor. (Refer to X-Ray Duplication Request for instructions.)
4. Give the patient an estimated fee for the necessary films.
Locate an appropriate appointment time on the schedule. Allow 1/2 hour for an FMX with an assis-
tant. (This procedure can be scheduled next to productive doctor time as long as an assistant and a
room are available.)
Enter the following basic patient information in the appointment book:
Last name, then first name. (i.e. Smith, Mary)
Work and home phone numbers.
Parents' work and home phone numbers, if patient is a minor.
Write "FMX" next to the patient's name to indicate the type of procedure scheduled.
Review the following information before ending the call:
Appointment date
Appointment time
Patient's phone number
Referring doctor, if applicable
Who will be obtaining the previous x-rays, if applicable
Directions to the office, if needed
8. If scheduling appointments for patients while they are in the office, complete an appointment card
with the appropriate appointment information. (7A-7B above)

全口 X 光检查 (FMX)

biting down on the film. This x-ray shows the dentist interproximal or recurrent cavities, calculus, over-
hanging restorations, crestal bone levels, internal pulpal pathology, and occlusal relationships. A BWX
series normally includes two or four posterior films.

use these films to help them interpret the current health and growth of the crown, root area, and surround-
ing bony structures.

unerupted, or impacted teeth are present. Some pediatric dentists will use occlusal x-rays in lieu of peri-
apical films.

plicable educational information and clearly understands the procedure prior to the

planned.
Measurement: Feedback from the patient, doctor, clinical assistants, and front
office staft:
Bleaching is a procedure performed to lighten the color of teeth. It is often desir-
able because it is the least invasive method of lightening the color of dark or dis-
colored teeth. Discoloration can be a result of an injury to the tooth causing hem-
orrhage; medications taken by the patient's mother during pregnancy; metallic re-
storative material; mottled enamel caused by fluorosis; intrinsic stains; the pa-
tient's age; consumption of coffee, tea, or nicotine. Bleaching can also be done
when a patient is dissatisfied with the current color of their teeth, before placement
of' a veneer to make the underlying tooth base more esthetically pleasing, and to
lighten natural teeth to match existing ceramic crowns or similar restorations. It is
extremely important that all patients are seen by the doctor in order to determine
whether or not the patient's current oral health can withstand bleaching treatment.
After the treatment is complete or post-delivery, follow-up contact with the patient
is necessary. Please refer to Treatment Follow-Up for instructions.

making the consultation appointment:

title: APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: EXTRACTIONS
text:
APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: EXTRACTIONS
SMILE STUDIO DENTISTRY
Desired Outcome: Appropriately schedule appointments to ensure quality care for patients in a timely,
stress-free manner. Patients seated on time and treatment completed as planned.
Measurement: Review of schedule. Feedback from patient, doctor, and clinical assistants.
A tooth extraction is the surgical removal of one or more teeth. There are two types of extractions: rou-
tine or simple extractions and surgical extractions. Simple extractions are often performed on a tooth that
is at least partially erupted and has a solid, intact crown. When conditions exist that require additional
skill and instrumentation to remove the tooth, a surgical extraction is performed. Surgical extractions can
also involve one or more of the following procedures during or after the extraction:
Removal of impacted teeth Ostectomy (removal of bone)
Mucoperiosteal flap removal
Tooth sectioning
Recovery of fractured roots
Soft tissue resection
1. Pull the patient's chart, if established. If there is a referring office, they will mail a prescription (R)
slip indicating which teeth are to be extracted. (We must have this slip before proceeding. The Rx
slip should be in the front pocket of chart on the appointment day.)
Ensure the patient understands why the doctor has recommended this treatment. If the patient does
not understand, after further explanation, notify the doctor and facilitate time for further explanation
directly from the doctor prior to receiving treatment.
3. Check the patient's dental insurance benefits. (Most dental insurance plans do cover extractions.)
A. If the patient requests a pre-determination of benefits be submitted to their insurance:
Refer to the corresponding SOP for instructions.
Ensure the patient understands that there is no guarantee with a pre-estimate and that
it takes 4-8 weeks for an estimate from the insurance carrier in writing.
4. Inform the patient of the fee and billing options:
$XX-complete a written estimate for the patient and keep a copy in the chart.
B. If financial arrangements are necessary, refer to the appropriate SOP for further instruction.
C. Forms of payment accepted personal check, credit card, etc.
Locate an appropriate date and time on the schedule-allow approximately one hour for the entire
appointment. Enter the following basic information in the appointment book:
Patient's last name, then first name (i.e. Smith, Mary).
Patient's work and home phone numbers (parent's, if patient is a minor).
Applicable tooth/teeth numbers) and "extract."
Block off chair time using the appropriate symbols for doctor and assistant time.
6. Complete an appointment card with the patient's name and appointment date/time. If scheduling the
appointment by phone, review the information before ending the call.
Document the appointment date and time in the patient's chart.
Consent toms

PROGRAMACIÓN DE CITA: EXTRACCIONES
SONRISA ESTUDIO ODONTOLOGÍA
Resultado deseado: programar citas adecuadamente para garantizar una atención de calidad para los pacientes de forma oportuna,
manera libre de estrés. Pacientes sentados a tiempo y tratamiento completado según lo planeado.
Medición: Revisión de cronograma. Comentarios de pacientes, médicos y asistentes clínicos.
Una extracción dental es la extracción quirúrgica de uno o más dientes. Hay dos tipos de extracciones:
extracciones de púas o simples y extracciones quirúrgicas. A menudo se realizan extracciones simples en un diente que
está al menos parcialmente en erupción y tiene una corona sólida e intacta. Cuando existen condiciones que requieren
habilidad e instrumentación para extraer el diente, se realiza una extracción quirúrgica. Las extracciones quirúrgicas pueden
También implican uno o más de los siguientes procedimientos durante o después de la extracción:
Extracción de dientes impactados Ostectomía (extracción de hueso)
Extirpación del colgajo mucoperióstico
seccionamiento de dientes
Recuperación de raíces fracturadas
Resección de tejidos blandos
1. Extraiga la ficha del paciente, si está establecida. Si hay una oficina de referencia, enviarán una receta por correo (R)
deslizamiento que indica qué dientes se van a extraer. (Debemos tener este recibo antes de continuar. El Rx
El recibo debe estar en el bolsillo delantero del expediente el día de la cita).
Asegúrese de que el paciente comprenda por qué el médico ha recomendado este tratamiento. Si el paciente lo hace
no entiende, después de más explicaciones, notifique al médico y dé tiempo para más explicaciones
directamente del médico antes de recibir el tratamiento.
3. Verifique los beneficios del seguro dental del paciente. (La mayoría de los planes de seguro dental cubren las extracciones).
A. Si el paciente solicita que se presente una predeterminación de beneficios a su seguro:
Consulte el POE correspondiente para obtener instrucciones.
Asegúrese de que el paciente comprenda que no hay garantía con un presupuesto previo y que
Se necesitan entre 4 y 8 semanas para obtener un presupuesto por escrito de la compañía de seguros.
4. Informar al paciente sobre la tarifa y las opciones de facturación:
$XX: complete un presupuesto escrito para el paciente y guarde una copia en el expediente.
B. Si son necesarios arreglos financieros, consulte el POE correspondiente para obtener más instrucciones.
C. Formas de pago aceptadas: cheque personal, tarjeta de crédito, etc.
Ubique una fecha y hora apropiadas en el cronograma; deje aproximadamente una hora para todo el
cita. Ingrese la siguiente información básica en el libro de citas:
Apellido del paciente, luego nombre (es decir, Smith, Mary).
Números de teléfono del trabajo y de casa del paciente (de los padres, si el paciente es menor de edad).
Números de diente/dientes aplicables) y "extracto".
Bloquee el tiempo en silla utilizando los símbolos apropiados para el tiempo del médico y del asistente.
6. Complete una tarjeta de cita con el nombre del paciente y la fecha/hora de la cita. Si programar el
cita por teléfono, revisar la información antes de finalizar la llamada.
Documente la fecha y hora de la cita en el expediente del paciente.
Consentimiento

DI VOMIT
APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: CROWN & BRIDGE
SMILE STUDIO DENTISTRY
Desired Outcome: Crown and bridge appointments scheduled accurately, allowing the appro-
priate amount of time for the procedure, Patient receives all applicable educational information
and clearly understands the procedure prior to the appointment. Patient arrives and is seated on
time and treatment is completed as planned.
Measurement: Feedback from the patient, doctor, clinical assistants, and front office staff.
Crowns and bridges are fixed oral prosthetics. A crown is usually a cast restoration or replica of
the entire anatomic crown of the tooth. A bridge is a series of artificial teeth (pontics) that are
supported by attaching them to abutment teeth. If a tooth cannot be restored to a functional level
with more conservative treatments, such as amalgams or composites, a crown and/or bridge may
be necessary. If the treatment plan documented in the patient's chart indicates the need for
crowns and/or bridges, follow the steps below to schedule the procedure.
1. Ensure the patient understands what a crown and/or bridge is and why the doctor has recom-
mended this treatment. (Refer to the information noted above.)
A. If the patient does not understand, after further explanation, notify the doctor and fa-
cilitate time for further explanation directly from the doctor prior to receiving treat-
Crown Prep and Delivery
1. Schedule a crown prep. If a post or build up is needed, allow 2 hours. (1 hr)
Check the patient's dental insurance benefits. (Most dental insurance plans do cover crowns
and bridges. However, all military retiree benefit programs do not.)
If the patient requests a Pre-Determination of Benefits be submitted to their insur-
ance, route the chart to bookkeeping and ensure the patient understands that there is
no guarantee with a pre-estimate and takes 4-8 weeks for an estimate from the insur-
ance carrier in writing.
3. Inform the patient of the fee and billing options:
$XX--complete a written estimate for the patient and keep a copy in the chart.
If financial arrangements are necessary, refer to the patient to bookkeeping.
C. Forms of payment accepted—-personal check, credit card, etc.
4. Enter the following information in the appointment book.
Patient's last name, then first name.
Patient's work and home phone numbers.
Tooth/teeth numbers).

PROGRAMACIÓN DE CITA: CORONA Y PUENTE
SONRISA ESTUDIO ODONTOLOGÍA
Resultado deseado: Las citas para coronas y puentes se programan con precisión, lo que permite
cantidad de tiempo adecuada para el procedimiento, el paciente recibe toda la información educativa aplicable
y comprende claramente el procedimiento antes de la cita. El paciente llega y se sienta en
tiempo y el tratamiento se completa según lo planeado.
Medición: Comentarios del paciente, médico, asistentes clínicos y personal de recepción.
Las coronas y puentes son prótesis bucales fijas. Una corona suele ser una restauración moldeada o una réplica de
toda la corona anatómica del diente. Un puente es una serie de dientes artificiales (pónticos) que se
apoyados uniéndolos a los dientes pilares. Si un diente no se puede restaurar a un nivel funcional
con tratamientos más conservadores, como amalgamas o composites, una corona y/o puente puede
ser necesario. Si el plan de tratamiento documentado en el expediente del paciente indica la necesidad de
coronas y/o puentes, siga los pasos a continuación para programar el procedimiento.
1. Asegúrese de que el paciente comprenda qué es una corona y/o puente y por qué el médico la ha recomendado.
Recomendó este tratamiento. (Consulte la información indicada anteriormente).
R. Si el paciente no comprende, después de más explicaciones, notifique al médico y a los familiares.

ance, enviar el cuadro a contabilidad y asegurarse de que el paciente entienda que hay

transportista por escrito.

Número de dientes/dientes).
