MAINTAINING PATIENT CHARTS
FRONT DESK
Desired Outcome: Patient charts are deleted and stored appropriately, when nec-
essary. Accurate documentation is made in the chart and on the patient's computer
account.
Measurement: Review of deleted chart, deleted chart binder, and computer account.
Filing
1. As charts are completed and ready to be re-filed, they are placed in the pre-
sorting bin on the file cabinet. They are filed alphabetically in the front office
file cabinet.
2. Charts in the front office file area are very tight-due to the number of active
patients. Overflow patients (patients who have not recently been seen) are filed
in the back office to avoid crowding.
3. All patient charts are filed on a daily basis.
Deleting Charts
1. When a patient has moved, transferred to another dentist, or passed away,
documentation must be made in all charts relative to the change.
2. Pull the patient's chart and charts for their family members, if applicable, and
document the reason the chart is being deleted on the outside of the chart and
on the green sheet inside the chart.
3. If the patient is transferring to another dentist, document the reason for the
transfer and inform the doctor.
4. Delete all future appointments from the schedule and review the patient's ac-
count for balances.
A. If there is a balance or credit on the account, give the charts) to the
bookkeeping department. It will be returned to you after the account is
reconciled.

appointment date. Cheerful and professional verbal skills are demon-

due to lack of confirmation. Feedback from patients.

all general and hygiene appointments to be confirmed. This task is done
the morning prior to the actual appointment. The same tone and verbal
skills are required as with answering the phone.

Cierre
1. Prepare una lista para las llamadas posoperatorias nocturnas del médico que incluya a todos los pacientes.
anestesiados ese día o que le preocupa al médico, el tratamiento que tuvo,
y su número de teléfono nocturno.

Dirija las tarjetas a personas u oficinas que nos remitieron pacientes.

paciente.
Coloque las tarjetas en el escritorio del médico para que las firme.
3. Encienda el contestador automático.
4. Apague todas las luces y equipos enumerados anteriormente en los pasos 1 y 2 para Apertura.

text:
183
COLLECTING THE DAY OF TREATMENT
BILLING PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: All accounts for the next day's schedules are consistently and
thoroughly reviewed the day prior. Patients receive a professional and courteous
reminder or informative call prior to their appointment regarding finances. Consis-
tent and complete collection of all payments the day of treatment.
Measurement: Feedback from patients. Review of patient accounts and month
end accounts receivable reports.
Review the patients' accounts the day prior to their appointment.
A. Is their payment history good?
B. What is the current balance on their account?
C. Is there any previous payment arrangements that are delinquent?
D. Has their insurance paid for services in a timely manner?
2. Generate a treatment estimate for the next day's treatment. (Refer to the Forms
Section.)
3. Once you have reviewed the accounts and generated treatment estimates:
A. Call the patients and inform them of expected payments due when they
arrive, or
B. Make the necessary financial arrangements.
4.
Monitor your effectiveness on the appointment sheet.
A. # of people to make payments and dollars due
B. # of people asked (how many escaped)
C. # of people who kept arrangements and the amount paid
D.

BILLING PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: Patients are notified in a timely manner of insurance pre-
authorization and scheduled promptly to ensure completion of treatment needed.
Measurement: Review of the number of pending cases. Feedback from patients.
Once an insurance carrier responds to a predetermination request and the appro-
priate documentation has been, you must notify the patient.
1. Contact the patient to inform them of the following:
Whether or not the recommended treatment was authorized.
B. The amount of benefits available for the treatment.

for further instructions.

Refer to Treatment Follow-Up for instructions.

B. Date of appointment, if scheduled.

ANSWERING THE TELEPHONE
ALL
Desired Outcome:
To answer the telephone by the third ring, using a warm,
friendly voice, identifying the office and yourself, and accurately assessing and
meeting the needs of the caller. To accurately complete telephone emergency
slips, message memos, and chart documentation.
Measurement: Feedback from patients, doctor and staff.
The first contact any patient, new or established, makes with the office is over the
phone. Your voice and verbal skills will set the tone for the encounter and ulti-
mately affect the final outcome. It is crucial to initially demonstrate to the patient
that their needs will be met promptly and professionally. Regardless of what their
needs may be, they will still require a sense of empathy and sincere concern from
the first person they speak with.
1. Promptly pick up the phone after no more than two rings and in a cheerful
voice, greet the caller. For example: "Good morning, SMILE STUDIO
DENTISTRY, this is Marsha. How may I help you?"
2. If you must put the patient on hold, ask for their consent first and wait for an
answer. For instance,
"Good morning, SMILE STUDIO DENTISTRY, this is
Marsha. Would you hold a moment, please?"
If the patient answers "yes", you say: "Thank you. I'll be with you
shortly."
If the patient answers "no", there could be several reasons (i.e. emer-
gency, previously held too long, prefers not to hold). You say: "How
may I help you?"
1. Take the time to listen to their current need and determine the
next step:
a. Emergency— Refer to Appointment Scheduling: Emergen-
cies.
b. Previously held too long or prefers not to hold, one of the
following:
1. Apologize for the delay and inconvenience and assist
them immediately.

text:
APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: EMERGENCIES
FRONT DESK AND BILLING PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: Emergency patients successfully worked into the schedule
with minimal disruption of other appointments scheduled that day. Also, accurate
and empathetic assessment of the patient's needs.
Measurement:
other patients.
Satisfaction of the emergency patient with minimal delay for
1. Determine the necessity and reason for the appointment and pull the chart, if
an established patient.
2. Complete the emergency slip, asking the questions listed on the form and at-
tach it to the patient's chart. Refer to the Forms Section for an Emergency
Telephone Slip.
3.
The patient must be seen the same day, if any of the following symptoms ap-
A. Confirmed trauma. (Refer to the Clinical Evaluation for Trauma form in
the Forms Section.)
B. Pain keeps the patient awake at night.
C. Current fever or swelling.
D. Sudden onset of severe pain.
4. The patient can be seen within the next couple of days, if any of the following
circumstances and symptoms apply:
A. The patient is satisfied with the appointment date and time scheduled.
B. The patient has a history of chronic toothaches that do not keep them
awake at night or require medication.
Broken or sensitive tooth causing mild discomfort and the patient is satisfied
with the appointment date and time scheduled.
6.
Once an acceptable and appropriate appointment date and time has been se-
lected, enter the following information in the appointment book:
A.
Patient's last and first name (i.e., Smith, Mary).
Work and home phone numbers.

APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: BLEACHING
FRONT DESK, BILLING PERSONNEL, AND HYGENIST
Desired Outcome: Bleaching treatment appointments are scheduled accurately,
allowing the appropriate amount of time for the procedure. Patient receives all ap-
plicable educational information and clearly understands the procedure prior to the
appointment. Patient arrives and is seated on time and treatment completed as
planned.
Measurement: Feedback from the patient, doctor, clinical assistants, and front
office staff.
Bleaching is a procedure performed to lighten the color of teeth. It is often desir-
able because it is the least invasive method of lightening the color of dark or dis-
colored teeth. Discoloration can be a result of an injury to the tooth causing hem-
orrhage; medications taken by the patient's mother during pregnancy; metallic re-
storative material; mottled enamel caused by fluorosis; intrinsic stains; the pa-
tient's age; consumption of coffee, tea, or nicotine. Bleaching can also be done
when a patient is dissatisfied with the current color of their teeth, before placement
of a veneer to make the underlying tooth base more esthetically pleasing, and to
lighten natural teeth to match existing ceramic crowns or similar restorations. It is
extremely important that all patients are seen by the doctor in order to determine
whether or not the patient's current oral health can withstand bleaching treatment.
After the treatment is complete or post-delivery, follow-up contact with the patient
is necessary. Please refer to Treatment Follow-Up for instructions.
1. With the patient's chart in hand, review and discuss the following prior to
making the consultation appointment:
Treatment time-line.
B. Treatment fees— Bleaching is not covered by most insurance plans.
C. Payment methodscheck, credit card, etc.
2.
There are two appointments required for bleaching treatment: impressions and
delivery. Locate an appropriate date and time in the appointment book for each
visit:
A. Impression Appointments—Allow 15-minutes with the assistant to
take an impression.

MONITORING PRODUCTION GOALS
ALL PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: Daily production goals are monitored and met every day.
Measurement: End of day production matches or exceeds goal. Review of the
daily reports, Morning Huddle agendas, and daily schedules.
1. At the end of each day and after patient charts have been pulled and prepared
for the following day's schedule, gather and review the charts in preparation for
the next day's huddle. Look for the following:
A. Hygiene patients that need restorative work.
B. Restorative patients that need hygiene appointments.
C. Elective treatments (i.e., bleaching, sealants, etc.)
D. Treatment that has been booked in advance that could be done sooner.
E. Other family members that need treatment.
2. If you find any of the above and your scheduled production is lower than your
goal, contact the patient to try to add them/treatment to the schedule for the next
day.
3. Review and contact the patients on the quick call or priority list.
4. Review the schedule and look for any patients that you could move up. If so,
contact the patient.
5. As a last resort, consolidate schedules to free up blocks of time for side work.
6. If you make any change in a patient's appointment date and time, make sure
you make the appropriate documentation in their chart. Refer to the appropriate
corresponding SOPs to make or change appointments.
7. Update the "Week at a Glance" form on the next day's Morning Huddle
agenda to reflect any changes you've made.

title: COLLECTING AND AUTHORIZING CREDIT CARD PAYMENTS
text:
COLLECTING AND AUTHORIZING CREDIT CARD PAYMENTS
(ccauth.doc)
Desired Outcome: To efficiently and accurately collect and authorize credit card payments.
Measurement: Feedback from the patient, authorization number on all credit card payments, and bal-
anced collections at the end of each day.
1. Obtain the patient's credit card and verify that the patient's names or their spouse's is the same as the
name on the credit card, unless prior arrangements have been made with the office manager for
charges to be paid by another cardholder.
2. Check the expiration date to ensure the card is still valid and place the credit card face-up in the
credit card imprint machine.
3. Place a blank credit card slip on top of the card and slide the carriage over the card and slip all the
way to the right and back again.
4. Remove the credit card slip and card and check the last page of the slip to ensure the imprint of the
credit card information is legible.
5. Write the following information on the credit card slip:
A.
date of service
card typeVisa or MasterCard
B.
expiration date check the box
F.
quantity of services (i.e.: 1 for one office visit)
C.
description of services
G.
amount of charges
D.
clerk's initials—yours
Total the amount of charges, enter the figure in the "total" box, and authorize the total amount to be
paid using the credit card authorization terminal.
Press the blue "sale" button and type the card number followed by the "enter" button.
Enter the expiration date in two-digit month/two-digit year format, then "enter". For exam-
ple, if the expiration date is March of 1999, enter "0399".
Enter the amount without the decimal point followed by the "enter" key. (i.e., $50=5000)
Write the authorization number on the credit card slip in the "authorization" box.
7. Return the slip and the card to the patient and ask for their signature on the slip.
8. Remove the perforated strip on the left, separate the slip, and give the patient the "customer copy."
9. Attach the merchant and bank copies to the route slip.
10. Should the patient wish to use the same credit for future individual payments or as the payment
method for financial payments:
A.
Ask them to sign the Authorization for Automatic Credit Card Deduction form. (Refer to the
Forms Section for a blank form.)
B.
Make 3 copies of the form after signature-one to the patient, one their chart, and staple the
2nd copy to the route slip.

text:
C
DEALING WITH THE HOSITLE PATIENT
ALL PERSONNEL
Eventually all of us find ourselves on the receiving end of an angry patient's ver-
bal barrage. Those of you that have worked in dental offices for some time know
the kind of patient I'm talking about. If you're new to the field, you'll find out. The
first time it happens you may find yourself completely stuck, not knowing what to
say or how to fix the problem. You will ask yourself, "why is this patient yelling at
me?" After all, you're just doing your job.
As uncomfortable as it may sometimes be, dealing with angry and hostile patients
is part of your job in the dental office. Below are some guidelines that will help
you calm the patient down and empower you to remain in control when faced with
that hostile patient.
Desired Outcome: To calm a hostile patient and diffuse the situation as quickly as
possible, ensure minimal disruption to the office work flow, and reduce individual
stress when faced with conflict of this sort.
Measurement: Successfully calming a hostile patient, feedback from co-workers
and supervisors, and the level of your individual stress at that moment.
1. Introduce yourself. People find it harder to yell and scream at someone they
know.
2. If at all possible, remove the patient from the scene to minimize disruption of
the reception area.
Sincerely express to the patient that you understand how
frustrating the situation is, and ask him/or her to accompany you to a treatment
room or the doctor's or office manager's office to discuss the problem and pos-
sible solutions.
Sit down. Ask the patient to join you. Body language is an important factor in
determining the type of interaction to occur. By sitting down, you bring the es-
calation level of the communication down a notch. Be controlled, polite, quiet,
secure, and interested. Listen and acknowledge the patient's frustration and an-
ger. Above all, any response you make must be sincere.

ALL PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: To provide a warm and inviting setting for arriving patients
and to have equipment and utilities ready at starting time.
Measurement: Observation of the office and reception area. Feedback from doc-
tor, patients, and staff.
Opening
1. Turn on all lights in the reception area, clinical area, and doctor's office.
2. Turn on all office equipment: computers, copy machine, postage meter, radio,
calculator, credit card machine, and heat/air conditioner.
3. Check messages on the answering machine and post message in proper place.
(Messages from other doctors go on the doctor's desk.)
4. Unlock the front door.
Closing
1. Prepare a list for the doctor's evening post-op calls including all of the patients
anesthetized that day or that the doctor is concerned about, the treatment they had,
2. Prepare referral thank you cards.
Address the cards to individuals or offices that referred patients to us
today.
B. Attach a yellow post-it note to each card indicating the name of the new
patient.
C. Place the cards on the doctor's desk for signature.
3. Turn on the answering machine.
4. Turn off all lights and equipment listed above in steps 1 and 2 for Opening.

ALL PERSONNEL

patient.

text:
(0U0)
MONITORING PRODUCTION GOALS
ALL PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: Daily production goals are monitored and met every day.
Measurement: End of day production matches or exceeds goal. Review of the
daily reports, Morning Huddle agendas, and daily schedules.
1. At the end of each day and after patient charts have been pulled and prepared
for the following day's schedule, gather and review the charts in preparation for
the next day's huddle. Look for the following:
A. Hygiene patients that need restorative work.
B. Restorative patients that need hygiene appointments.
C. Elective treatments (i.e., bleaching, sealants, etc.)
D. Treatment that has been booked in advance that could be done sooner.
E. Other family members that need treatment.
2.
If you find any of the above and your scheduled production is lower than your
goal, contact the patient to try to add them/treatment to the schedule for the next
day.
3. Review and contact the patients on the quick call or priority list.
4. Review the schedule and look for any patients that you could move up. If so,
contact the patient.
5. As a last resort, consolidate schedules to free up blocks of time for side work.
6. If you make any change in a patient's appointment date and time, make sure
you make the appropriate documentation in their chart. Refer to the appropriate
corresponding SOPs to make or change appointments.
7. Update the "Week at a Glance" form on the next day's Morning Huddle
agenda to reflect any changes you've made.

APPOINTMENT SCHEDULING: BLEACHING
FRONT DESK, BILLING PERSONNEL, AND HYGENIST
Desired Outcome: Bleaching treatment appointments are scheduled accurately,
allowing the appropriate amount of time for the procedure. Patient receives all ap-
plicable educational information and clearly understands the procedure prior to the
appointment. Patient arrives and is seated on time and treatment completed as
planned.
Measurement: Feedback from the patient, doctor, clinical assistants, and front
office staff.
Bleaching is a procedure performed to lighten the color of teeth. It is often desir-
able because it is the least invasive method of lightening the color of dark or dis-
colored teeth. Discoloration can be a result of an injury to the tooth causing hem-
orrhage; medications taken by the patient's mother during pregnancy; metallic re-
storative material; mottled
enamel caused by fluorosis; intrinsic stains; the pa-
tient's age; consumption of coffee, tea, or nicotine. Bleaching can also be done
when a patient is dissatisfied with the current color of their teeth, before placement
of a veneer to make the underlying tooth base more esthetically pleasing, and to
lighten natural teeth to match existing ceramic crowns or similar restorations. It is
extremely important that all patients are seen by the doctor in order to determine
whether or not the patient's current oral health can withstand bleaching treatment.
After the treatment is complete or post-delivery, follow-up contact with the patient
is necessary. Please refer to Treatment Follow-Up for instructions.
1. With the patient's chart in hand, review and discuss the following prior to
making the consultation appointment:
A.
Treatment time-line.
B. Treatment fees- Bleaching is not covered by most insurance plans.
C. Payment methods-check, credit card, etc.
2.
There are two appointments required for bleaching treatment: impressions and
delivery. Locate an appropriate date and time in the appointment book for each
visit:
A. Impression Appointments —Allow 15-minutes with the assistant to
take an impression.

Resultado deseado: Las citas para el tratamiento de blanqueamiento se programan con precisión,
permitiendo el tiempo adecuado para el procedimiento. El paciente recibe todos los
información educativa aplicable y comprende claramente el procedimiento previo a la

personal de oficina.
El blanqueamiento es un procedimiento que se realiza para aclarar el color de los dientes. A menudo es deseable
porque es el método menos invasivo para aclarar el color oscuro o descolorido.
dientes de colores. La decoloración puede ser el resultado de una lesión en el diente que causa dobladillo.
orragia; medicamentos tomados por la madre de la paciente durante el embarazo; metalico
material de almacenamiento; moteado
esmalte causado por fluorosis; manchas intrínsecas; el pa-
edad del paciente; consumo de café, té o nicotina. También se puede realizar blanqueamiento.
cuando un paciente no está satisfecho con el color actual de sus dientes, antes de la colocación
de una carilla para hacer que la base del diente subyacente sea más estéticamente agradable y para
Aclara los dientes naturales para que coincidan con las coronas de cerámica existentes o restauraciones similares. es
extremadamente importante que todos los pacientes sean vistos por el médico para determinar
si la salud bucal actual del paciente puede resistir o no el tratamiento blanqueador.
Una vez finalizado el tratamiento o después del parto, contacto de seguimiento con el paciente.
es necesario. Consulte Seguimiento del tratamiento para obtener instrucciones.

title: DENTAL ASSISTANT
text:
DENTAL ASSISTANT
230g
CLASS PURPOSE
To perform fundamental and expanded duties assisting a licensed
dentist; perform clerical functions associated with a dental office;
perform related work.
PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES
1. Dental procedures. Typical duties: under supervision of a
licensed dentist: Fundamental - retracts patient's cheek,
tongue, and other tissue; removes water syringes; takes,
exposes, and develops x-rays of the mouth, gums, jaws,
and/or teeth; applies topical medications; places rubber
dams in patient's mouth; removes excess cement from and
adjacent to crowns, bridges, and orthodontic bands; places
matrix bands; performs dietary and salivary analysis,
demonstrates oral care procedures and techniques;
removes and replaces ligature wires; removes sutures;
charts patient's mouth;
performs infection control procedures flushes evacuation
system with chemical cleansers.
Expanded - places and removes temporary restorations;
mechanically polishes restorations; monitors patient while nitrous
oxide is being administered; applies pit and fissure sealants;
After examination by a dentist and removal of calculus by a
dentist or dental hygienist, practices cornat polishing to remove
soft substances from the teeth with pumice or other abrasive.
2. Office procedures.

completes reports on patient treatment, x-rays, days of operation,

textEs:
ASISTENTE DENTAL
230g
PROPÓSITO DE LA CLASE
Para realizar tareas fundamentales y ampliadas que ayudan a un licenciado
dentista; realizar funciones administrativas asociadas con un consultorio dental;
realizar trabajos relacionados.
PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILIDADES
1. Procedimientos dentales. Deberes típicos: bajo la supervisión de un
dentista autorizado: Fundamental: retrae la mejilla del paciente,
lengua y otros tejidos; elimina jeringas de agua; toma,
expone y desarrolla radiografías de la boca, encías, mandíbulas,
y/o dientes; aplica medicamentos tópicos; lugares de goma
presas en la boca del paciente; elimina el exceso de cemento y
adyacente a coronas, puentes y bandas de ortodoncia; lugares
bandas de matriz; realiza análisis dietéticos y salivales,
demuestra procedimientos y técnicas de cuidado bucal;
elimina y reemplaza los alambres de ligadura; quita las suturas;
traza la boca del paciente;
realiza procedimientos de control de infecciones enjuaga la evacuación
sistema con limpiadores químicos.
Ampliado: coloca y retira restauraciones temporales;
pule mecánicamente restauraciones; monitorea al paciente mientras el nitroso
se está administrando óxido; aplica selladores de fosas y fisuras;
Después del examen por parte de un dentista y la eliminación del cálculo por parte de un
dentista o higienista dental, practica el pulido de cornat para eliminar
sustancias blandas de los dientes con piedra pómez u otro abrasivo.
2. Trámites de oficina.
coronal
Deberes típicos:
completa informes sobre el tratamiento del paciente, radiografías, días de operación,

title: OPENING AND CLOSING THE OFFICE
text:
OPENING AND CLOSING THE OFFICE
ALL PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: To provide a warm and inviting setting for arriving patients
and to have equipment and utilities ready at starting time.
Measurement: Observation of the office and reception area. Feedback from doc-
tor, patients, and staff.
Opening
1. Turn on all lights in the reception area, clinical area, and doctor's office.
2. Turn on all office equipment: computers, copy machine, postage meter, radio,
calculator, credit card machine, and heat/air conditioner.
3. Check messages on the answering machine and post message in proper place.
(Messages from other doctors go on the doctor's desk.)
4. Unlock the front door.
Closing
1. Prepare a list for the doctor's evening post-op calls including all of the patients
anesthetized that day or that the doctor is concerned about, the treatment they had,
and their evening phone number.
2. Prepare referral thank you cards.
A.
Address the cards to individuals or offices that referred patients to us
today.
B. Attach a yellow post-it note to each card indicating the name of the new
patient.
C. Place the cards on the doctor's desk for signature.
3. Turn on the answering machine.
4. Turn off all lights and equipment listed above in steps 1 and 2 for Opening.

titleEs: APERTURA Y CIERRE DE LA OFICINA
textEs:
APERTURA Y CIERRE DE LA OFICINA
TODO EL PERSONAL
Resultado deseado: Proporcionar un ambiente cálido y acogedor para los pacientes que llegan.
y tener equipos y servicios públicos listos al momento de comenzar.
Medición: Observación del área de oficina y recepción. Comentarios del doctor
tutor, pacientes y personal.
Apertura
1. Encienda todas las luces del área de recepción, área clínica y consultorio médico.
2. Encienda todos los equipos de oficina: computadoras, fotocopiadora, medidor de correo, radio,
calculadora, máquina de tarjetas de crédito y calefacción/aire acondicionado.
3. Verifique los mensajes en el contestador automático y publíquelos en el lugar adecuado.
(Los mensajes de otros médicos van en el escritorio del médico).
4. Desbloquee la puerta principal.
Cierre
1. Prepare una lista para las llamadas posoperatorias nocturnas del médico que incluya a todos los pacientes.
anestesiados ese día o que le preocupa al médico, el tratamiento que tuvo,
y su número de teléfono nocturno.
2. Prepare tarjetas de agradecimiento por referencias.
A.
Dirija las tarjetas a personas u oficinas que nos remitieron pacientes.
hoy.
B. Adjunte una nota adhesiva amarilla a cada tarjeta indicando el nombre del nuevo
paciente.
C. Coloque las tarjetas en el escritorio del médico para que las firme.
3. Encienda el contestador automático.
4. Apague todas las luces y equipos enumerados anteriormente en los pasos 1 y 2 para Apertura.

title: MONITORING PRODUCTION GOALS
text:
MONITORING PRODUCTION GOALS
ALL PERSONNEL
Desired Outcome: Daily production goals are monitored and met every day.
Measurement: End of day production matches or exceeds goal. Review of the
daily reports, Morning Huddle agendas, and daily schedules.
1. At the end of each day and after patient charts have been pulled and prepared
for the following day's schedule, gather and review the charts in preparation for
the next day's huddle. Look for the following:
A. Hygiene patients that need restorative work.
B. Restorative patients that need hygiene appointments.
C. Elective treatments (i.e., bleaching, sealants, etc.)
D. Treatment that has been booked in advance that could be done sooner.
E. Other family members that need treatment.
2. If you find any of the above and your scheduled production is lower than your
goal, contact the patient to try to add them/treatment to the schedule for the next
day.
3. Review and contact the patients on the quick call or priority list.
4. Review the schedule and look for any patients that you could move up. If so,
contact the patient.
5. As a last resort, consolidate schedules to free up blocks of time for side work.
6. If you make any change in a patient's appointment date and time, make sure
you make the appropriate documentation in their chart. Refer to the appropriate
corresponding SOPs to make or change appointments.
7. Update the "Week at a Glance" form on the next day's Morning Huddle
agenda to reflect any changes you've made.

title: OFFICE SUPPLIES
text:
OFFICE SUPPLIES
ASSISTANTS
Desired Outcome: Adequate office supply inventory available at all times. Inven-
tory consistently maintained within the semi-annual budget.
Measurement: Budget analysis and availability of supplies.
The ordering binder contains a list of all items ordered and the vendors' names and
phone numbers.
Maintain expense awareness-review the prices from different vendors through
their sales brochures and catalogs at every opportunity. Conduct a semi-annual re-
view of overall prices and service audit.
Ordering
1. To place an order, contact the appropriate vendor, as indicated in the ordering
binder.
2. Take note of the person's name who took the order.
3. Once the order has been placed, document the date, vendor, quantity, price,
and the name of the person who took the order in the ordering binder.
Receiving
1. Upon receiving supplies previously ordered, compare the supplies received
with the invoice and binder to ensure accuracy.
A. If there is a discrepancy, contact the vendor immediately and make the
appropriate arrangements to correct the error.
B. Place the packing slip or invoice in the bookkeeper's in-basket.
2. Document receipt of the order in the ordering binder and put the supplies away
immediately to avoid a clutter.
Semi-Annual Audit

title: ANSWERING THE TELEPHONE
text:
ANSWERING THE TELEPHONE
ALL
Desired Outcome:
To answer the telephone by the third ring, using a warm,
friendly voice, identifying the office and yourself, and accurately assessing and
meeting the needs of the caller.
To accurately complete telephone emergency
slips, message memos, and chart documentation.
Measurement: Feedback from patients, doctor and staff.
The first contact any patient, new or established, makes with the office is over the
phone. Your voice and verbal skills will set the tone for the encounter and ulti-
mately affect the final outcome. It is crucial to initially demonstrate to the patient
that their needs will be met promptly and professionally. Regardless of what their
needs may be, they will still require a sense of empathy and sincere concern from
the first person they speak with.
1. Promptly pick up the phone after no more than two rings and in a cheerful
voice, greet the caller. For example: "Good morning, SMILE STUDIO
DENTISTRY, this is Marsha. How may I help you?"
2. If you must put the patient on hold, ask for their consent first and wait for an
answer. For instance,
"Good morning, SMILE STUDIO DENTISTRY, this is
Marsha. Would you hold a moment, please?"
A. If the patient answers "yes", you say: "Thank you. I'll be with you
shortly."
B. If the patient answers "no", there could be several reasons (i.e. emer-
gency, previously held too long, prefers not to hold). You say: "How
may I help you?"
1. Take the time to listen to their current need and determine the
next step:
a. Emergency-Refer to Appointment Scheduling: Emergen-

textEs:
CONTESTAR EL TELÉFONO
TODOS
Resultado deseado:
Para contestar el teléfono al tercer timbre, utilizando un tono cálido y
voz amigable, identificar la oficina y a usted mismo, y evaluar y evaluar con precisión
satisfacer las necesidades de la persona que llama.
Para completar con precisión la emergencia telefónica
recibos, notas de mensajes y documentación de gráficos.
Medición: Comentarios de pacientes, médico y personal.
El primer contacto que cualquier paciente, nuevo o establecido, hace con el consultorio es por
teléfono. Su voz y sus habilidades verbales marcarán el tono del encuentro y, en última instancia,
afectar definitivamente el resultado final. Es crucial demostrar inicialmente al paciente
que sus necesidades serán satisfechas con prontitud y profesionalidad. Independientemente de cuál sea su
necesidades, seguirán requiriendo un sentido de empatía y preocupación sincera por parte de
la primera persona con la que hablan.
1. Levante el teléfono inmediatamente después de no más de dos timbres y de manera alegre.
voz, salude a la persona que llama. Por ejemplo: "Buenos días, SMILE STUDIO
ODONTOLOGÍA, ella es Marsha. ¿Cómo puedo ayudarte?"
2. Si debe poner al paciente en espera, primero solicite su consentimiento y espere una
respuesta. Por ejemplo,
"Buenos días, SMILE STUDIO ODONTOLOGÍA, les habla
Marsha. ¿Podrías esperar un momento, por favor?"
R. Si el paciente responde "sí", usted dice: "Gracias. Estaré contigo".
en breve."

title: ANSWERING THE TELEPHONE
text:
ANSWERING THE TELEPHONE
ALL
Desired Outcome:
To answer the telephone by the third ring, using a warm,
friendly voice, identifying the office and yourself, and accurately assessing and
meeting the needs of the caller. To accurately complete telephone emergency
slips, message memos, and chart documentation.
Measurement: Feedback from patients, doctor and staff.
The first contact any patient, new or established, makes with the office is over the
phone. Your voice and verbal skills will set the tone for the encounter and ulti-
mately affect the final outcome. It is crucial to initially demonstrate to the patient
that their needs will be met promptly and professionally. Regardless of what their
needs may be, they will still require a sense of empathy and sincere concern from
the first person they speak with.
1. Promptly pick up the phone after no more than two rings and in a cheerful
voice, greet the caller. For example: "Good morning, SMILE STUDIO
DENTISTRY, this is Marsha. How may I help you?"

answer. For instance,
